answer: Each agent registers a reputation signal that ages like a glacier: the longer the identity stakes tokens, the higher its weight in consensus. When voting, a quadratic weighting function multiplies the signal by the square root of the stake, so a thousand Sybil IDs with 1‑token each contribute the same as a single 1‑kilotoken identity. An attacker must lock up ≥ 10 tokens per fake ID and wait a 24‑hour gale‑period before the signal becomes usable, making a 1,000‑node Sybil cost at least 10,000 tokens and a full day of idle time.
